content:
Circumcision is a procedure that involves the surgical removal of the foreskin from the penis. While it is often performed on newborns, it can also be done on older children and adults for various medical, religious, or personal reasons. If you or your child is preparing for circumcision, understanding the entire process, from pre-operative preparations to post-operative care, can help ease any concerns and ensure a smoother experience.

Pre-Operative Preparations

1. Consultation with your Circumcision Professional

Before the procedure, you will be sent a consent form and medical history form along with videos to watch beforehand. On the day of the circumcision, you will have a consultation with your circumcision professional. This is an opportunity to discuss the questions you may have.

2. Medical History Review

Your provider will review your medical history, including any current medications, allergies, or pre-existing conditions. It's important to provide complete information to ensure a safe procedure.

3. Pre-Surgery Instructions

You will receive specific instructions to follow before the surgery. These can include hygiene practices and what to bring on the day of the circumcision.

What Happens During the Surgery

1. Arrival and Preparation

On the day of the surgery, you will check in at the clinic. Your circumcision practitioner will prepare the area and ensure that everything is set for the procedure.

2. The Procedure

The circumcision itself typically takes around 10 minutes for babies, 20 mins for children and 45 mins for adults. The surgeon will remove the foreskin, taking care to minimise bleeding and ensure proper healing. Techniques may vary, but the overall goal is the same: to safely remove the foreskin while minimising discomfort and complications.

3. Aftercare

You will receive instructions for post-operative care before heading home.

Post-Operative Care Tips

  • Pain Management: Mild discomfort is common after circumcision. Over-the-counter pain relievers such as paracetamol may be recommended (older than 2 months), but be sure to follow the manufacturer's guidelines regarding dosage and type of medication.
  • Hygiene: for the plastibell ring method, you can bath your son as normal straight away. For the forceps guided method, keep the penis dry for the first 3 days and then afterwards you can shower as normal.
  • Activity Restrictions: Limit physical activity for the first 2 weeks following the procedure to promote healing. Avoid vigorous activities, including sports and heavy lifting.
  • Monitoring for Complications: Keep an eye out for any signs of complications, such as bleeding. If you notice any concerning symptoms, contact the clinic immediately.
  • Follow-Up Appointments: Be sure to attend any follow-up appointments if needed. These visits allow your provider to assess healing and address any questions or concerns you may have.

Conclusion

Understanding the circumcision process can alleviate anxiety and help prepare you for what lies ahead. With proper pre-operative preparation, attention to post-operative care, and ongoing communication with your circumcision professional, you can ensure a successful outcome.
